jobs.description:
**Job Description

**HO Finance oversees accounting, tax, treasury, controlling and internal controls — driving value through financial stewardship, compliance, and forward-looking support. The role requires on top, a good understanding of the company's ERP and financial system interfaces, together with IFRS and Local Danish Gaap knowledge.

This person will be the backbone of Finance, making sure tight deadlines are met in a timely manner and in quality.

**Your Main Responsibilities Will Be

**

• Lead a high performance multicultural accounting team consisting of Accounts receivable, Accounts payable, general ledger, controlling and customs.

• Ensure proper accounting, reporting and complete, timely and consistent financial accuracy of all records and assets.

• Provide management with periodic financial reports and analyses for management decision-making.

• Ensure an effective internal control environment.

• Support operations through responsibility of: accounting and financial reporting, month-end close, tax, internal controls, cash and debt management, working capital management, insurance, and risk management.

• Cooperation with external auditors for the annual reports in Satair DK and Satair UK incl. local tax computations and tax-reporting to authorities.

• Cooperation with internal auditors from Airbus Group.

Travel days to be expected are 2-4 yearly travels to Hamburg and Toulouse, 1-2 trips to UK as necessary.

**How You Will Contribute To The Team

**You will be required to apply business experience, judgement and compliance knowledge to provide added value for the business therefore we are looking for a person with a Masters degree or similar education with a minimum of 5 years at a middle or senior level in a financial management function, preferably in a global wholesale/distribution organization or audit.

Good analytical skills; ability to see the bigger picture and derive mid to long term recommendations on the way forward to stakeholders and excellent communication skills is a must. Teamplayer and the ability to balance and align varying interests of stakeholders is a key feature to master in this position.

A digital mindset, proficient in SAP or similar business management system and mastery of Google suite solutions and AI preferred.

As the company language is English, excellent command of both written and spoken English is a must.

**What does your next challenge look like?

**At SATAIR, we believe in sustainable aviation that allows people to travel and connect across the globe.

We are on a mission to provide world class material solutions that keep aircraft flying and extend their lifespan.

In Satair, you can challenge the status quo, pioneer new ways of working, and generate real value for airlines and suppliers worldwide.

Being part of the Airbus family gives us the opportunity to live a global mindset, working in international and diverse teams and collaborating across functions, sites and cultures.

If you want to work as one team embracing a can-do attitude in a demanding environment, then we offer a great place to explore, learn, and grow, making an impact on aviation’s digital and sustainable transformation.

_Come on board and join us at Satair, an Airbus Services Company!

_**About SATAIR

**Satair is an Airbus Services company offering first-class material management solutions in the aviation aftermarket industry. We take pride in delivering an excellent customer experience around the clock, driving innovation, and contributing to aviation’s digital and sustainable transformation.

With our global functional organisation spanning 12 sites and locations worldwide, and a team of over 2,000 people supporting a $3.9 billion turnover, you will be part of a truly global company that continues to grow year after year.

Welcome to the Satair family!

If you want to know more about our business, have a closer look at our website www.SATAIR.com or check out our SATAIR Youtube Channel at www.youtube.com/sataircompany !

**What do we offer at SATAIR?

**At SATAIR, you will find much more than a job - we offer you the possibility of growing both your personal and professional capacities in a fun, supportive and informal working environment, where you will be encouraged to engage, share knowledge and ideas.

SATAIR is committed to achieving workforce diversity and creating an inclusive working environment. We love to bring in people with different backgrounds and experiences as we believe it enhances our performance immensely!

Here is a selection of some of the benefits we offer our employees in Copenhagen:

Financial Benefits: Competitive salary, Employee Stock Ownership Program, Success sharing, Health insurance, Group accident insurance, Employee discounts to local businesses

Employee Health and Wellbeing: On-site gym, App-based health & wellbeing platform, Amazing canteen at a subsided price, Massage scheme

Learning and Development: Airbus Leadership University, Large number of e-learning and training offers for personal and professional development, Promotion of professional development (e.g. postgraduate studies, technician training), Possibility of mentoring, Gain international experience

Work-life blend and life phase support: Possibility to work remotely, 4 care days, Senior days, Working from home policy (2 days remote per week)

**Come on board and join us at Satair, an Airbus Services Company

**Please send us your application no later than 30. November 2026 to get the opportunity to become part of an exceptional global team!

We welcome all applications irrespective of social and cultural background, age, gender, disability, sexual orientation or religious belief.

When applying for the position, you accept our data privacy statement: _http://www.SATAIR.com/privacy

_This job requires an awareness of any potential compliance risks and a commitment to act with integrity, as the foundation for the Company’s success, reputation and sustainable growth.

Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

We are looking for a Data Regulation Counsel to support Veo’s work within data protection and emerging technology regulation. You will play a key role in the day-to-day operation of Veo’s compliance framework and help ensure that our products, services, development, and internal processes meet applicable regulatory requirements.

You will join the Legal Team, currently consisting of four full-time employees, and work closely with it, as well as colleagues across IT, Marketing, Product, and other business areas. While the role's primary focus is GDPR compliance, your tasks will also include operational compliance related to NIS2, the Data Act, the Cyber Resilience Act, and the AI Act.

This is a unique opportunity to join a growing Legal function and help build scalable, pragmatic compliance processes at a company experiencing significant growth and continuous development.

**You can expect tasks within a variety of areas, including:

**

• Supporting the implementation and day-to-day operation of Veo’s data regulation compliance framework, ensuring that established processes are followed and continuously improved.

• Assisting in ensuring that Veo’s products, services, and internal data processing activities comply with applicable data regulation requirements.

• Providing practical and solution-oriented support to teams across Veo on data regulation matters, with a focus on translating legal requirements into operational processes.

• Drafting, updating, and maintaining relevant policies, procedures, and documentation, including privacy notices, records of processing activities, transfer impact assessments, incident response procedures, and documentation required under the regulatory frameworks.

• Supporting the handling of operational compliance tasks, including data subject rights requests, personal data breaches, and security incidents.

• Contributing to drafting and facilitating training and awareness initiatives.

• Supporting the management of third-party relationships from a compliance perspective, including assisting with due diligence, contractual requirements, and ongoing monitoring.

• Contributing to the ongoing monitoring, development, optimization, and, where relevant, automation of compliance processes, ensuring that Veo’s approach remains scalable and aligned with business needs.

Previous experience with all of the above is not required.

**Your qualifications:

**

• A master’s degree in law or business law from a Nordic university.

• Solid experience with advising on GDPR and/or other data regulation. Experience from scale ups or law firms is an advantage but not required..

• An interest in and basic understanding of broader technology regulation (e.g. NIS2, AI Act, Data Act).

• A pragmatic and structured approach to problem-solving and the ability to translate legal requirements into commercial and operational solutions.

• An interest in working closely with stakeholders across different functions and with varying professional backgrounds.

• A solid understanding of and interest in technology and artificial intelligence.

• The ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities in a dynamic environment.

• Strong communication skills in English, both written and spoken.

At Veo, the Legal Team is part of the Finance Department, and you will report to the Head of Legal. In your day-to-day work, you will collaborate closely with our experienced Data Protection Counsel. We offer an informal working environment where individual contributions are highly valued, both professionally and socially. We encourage personal and professional development while providing a flexible work environment, even during busy periods.

Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

Play as a team - We collaborate across a diverse organization, leveraging shared insights for stronger

outcomes.

Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally)

We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, even if your experience doesn’t completely match every qualification listed. What matters most is your creativity, potential, and ability to make meaningful contributions.

💰 Salary, based on experience level: 🇬🇧 London - up to £92 000 a year/gross 🇩🇰 Copenhagen - up to 74 000 DKK a month/gross

Intro

Monta powers the EV charging ecosystem. With 300,000+ monthly users and millions of charge sessions every month, our platform accelerates the electrification of mobility.

This is a fast-moving place. The problems are hard, the pace is quick, and the bar is high. If you like real ownership, figuring things out, and seeing the direct impact of your work, you'll do well with us.

AI is built into how we work. It helps us ship faster, make better decisions, and stay lean. Everyone at Monta is expected to use AI tools thoughtfully — and to find smart ways to use them to move the work forward.

Our principles keep us grounded: Build Together & Finish, Sweat the Details, Customer First, and Aim for the Moon.

The best part of Monta is the people — sharp, ambitious, and good to be around. You'll be challenged, supported, and trusted to deliver.

We're looking for a Solution Engineer who's ready to roll up their sleeves, take ownership, and build with us — through the grind and the wins. You'll be the technical partner to our Sales team: you work out what customers need, show them how Monta solves it, and make sure what we sell can be delivered.

This Is What You Will Achieve

• Win the technical decision — be the reason charge point operators, energy companies and fleet owners choose Monta to run their charging business.

• Make sure what we sell gets delivered — the commitments made during the sale are realistic and land cleanly with our implementation team.

• Shape the product — turn what you hear from customers into clear input that Product and Engineering can act on.

What You Will Do

• Lead technical discovery — understand the customer's business, their current charging setup (platform, hardware, roaming, billing) and what they need to integrate with.

• Run demos built around the customer — tailored to their use cases, not a feature tour.

• Design the solution — define the high-level architecture and integration approach, from OCPP chargers and OCPI roaming to APIs, ERP and energy management.

• Lead proofs of concept and technical evaluations — agree scope and success criteria up front and see them through to sign-off.

• Answer the hard questions — technical, architecture, integration and security questions in meetings, RFPs and security questionnaires.

• Spot risk early — flag gaps and dependencies before a deal is committed, and push back when a promise can't be kept.

• Partner with Sales — on the technical strategy for complex, multi-country deals.

• Hand over cleanly — give the Solution Architect a documented scope so implementation starts on solid ground.

• Close the loop with Product — feed recurring requirements and product gaps back to Product and Engineering.

• Help post-sales when it's busy — for example scoping a migration or running a technical workshop with a live customer.

What We're Looking For

• Experience in a customer-facing technical role — as a Solution Engineer, Sales Engineer or pre-sales consultant, selling B2B software or platform products.

• You explain technical topics clearly to non-technical people — and can go deep with the customer's engineers in the same meeting.

• Your discovery gets to the real problem — you ask the question behind the requirement before proposing a solution.

• You build demos that tell the customer's story — you're comfortable changing course live when the conversation goes somewhere new.

• Hands-on with APIs and integrations — you can read API docs, test calls yourself, and explain web-hooks, authentication and data flows.

• Commercial awareness — you understand how deals are won and lost, and you know when to protect scope.

• You write clearly — solution designs, RFP answers and handover notes that others can act on without a follow-up call.

• EV charging, energy or mobility knowledge is a plus (OCPP, OCPI, load management), but not required. We'll teach you the domain.

• You use AI to work faster — for example on RFP drafts, research, demo prep and documentation, and you check the output before it reaches a customer.

• Fluent English, and happy to travel to customer workshops around Europe from time to time.

**_If the mission excites you but your experience isn't a perfect 1:1 match, apply anyway — we care about potential, not perfection.

_**Why Monta

• Impact, not easy mode — your work matters, and you'll feel it every day.

• Ownership from day one — we don't micromanage, we expect you to deliver.

• The grind is real — priorities shift, and flexibility is sometimes needed to get things across the finish line. But so are the rewards: impact, growth, and a team that has your back.

• The people are extraordinary — talented, driven, and fun to work with. You'll be challenged, supported, and inspired in equal measure.

What We Offer

• A yearly education budget and extra days off to use it.

• A friendly and social company culture with movie nights, Friday bars, pub crawls, and more.

• Free lunch every day.

• Pension & health coverage to keep you secure for today and tomorrow.

• Paid parental leave to support life's big moments.

• Warrants program - be part of our growth story.

• Flexible working hours; as long as you're at key meetings and delivering great work, we trust you to manage your schedule.

**Please send us your application in English.

**To succeed in this position, your spoken and written English skills need to be proficient. Since Monta is a globally active company, you'll be communicating often and regularly with our co-workers and partners around the world, making your professional English knowledge essential.

Please note that we don't accept unsolicited applications from headhunters or recruitment agencies. Unsolicited applications sent to our company or co-workers are considered to be the property of Monta, and we won't agree to pay any referral compensation or recruiter fee without a signed agreement.

Find out more by visiting https://monta.com/uk/careers/

**Job Description

****Senior Product Owner

**Join us as we transform banking through data at Danske Bank. As Product Owner for Data Products, ML Enablement and MLops, you will help shape the future of personal banking by creating scalable data assets that power personalized customer experiences. This is your opportunity to lead meaningful change in financial services.

You will join the Customer Engagement Individuals Tribe as a Senior Product Owner with responsibility for driving the work needed to succeed with our strategy, together with, Engineers, Business Functional Specialists, Architects and more. In our department you will gain approximately 160 colleagues where you will lead one of the squads who will help enable Danske Bank to get ready for the next generation of banking services.

**You will lead a diverse team of data engineers, architects, and specialists across the Customer Engagement Individuals tribe, working on the group-wide AWS Databricks platform. Your work directly enables proactive, personalized banking services that build lasting customer relationships.

• Break down strategic priorities into vision and purpose for the team

• Drive the work leading leading to materialization of north star vision

• Lead development of data assets and products for commercial use cases

• Collaborate with data platform teams and deploy advanced analytics models using MLOps practices

• Manage stakeholders across the bank working with data development

• Guide conversion of PC platform to the group-wide data platform

**

Building AI keeps getting cheaper and faster. Deciding what's worth building, and getting an organisation to actually commit to it, does not.

At Heyra, we build AI systems, workflows and data platforms that are meant to live in production from day one. We work closely with companies that are moving quickly and need a partner who can hold both the strategic picture and the delivery reality in one head.

We're looking for a Deployment Strategist: the person the client's leadership talks to. You own the relationship and the outcome. You sit with a C-suite buyer, understand where their business is actually trying to go, and translate that into a sharp, sequenced plan for what we build and why. Then you steer a strong engineering team to make it real - without being the one in the codebase.

This is the strategic counterpart to our engineers. Where they go deep into the build, you hold the commercial and strategic frame: what problem are we really solving, what impact are we creating, in what order, and how do we get the organisation to adopt it. You're more product manager than a traditional consultant, with a strong strategic angle - closer to an Engagement Manager who's technical enough to make the right calls than a slide-deck advisor.

You'll work closely with engineers, data specialists, strategists and designers in a company where ideas move quickly and the distance from thinking to building is intentionally small.

What you'll work on

• Owning client relationships at the leadership level - being the person the C-suite trusts

• Framing the real problem behind the ask, and shaping it into an engagement worth running together with our FDEs

• Sequencing what gets built, in what order, and being accountable for the business value - not just the artifact

• Steering engineering teams toward outcomes, translating in both directions between the client and the builders

• Driving adoption: managing expectations, working with the people who have to live with the solution, and staying through the part after launch

• Scoping, structuring and de-risking engagements as they evolve

• Spotting where the next opportunity sits inside an account and growing it

**Requirements

****You probably have experience with

**

• Management consulting, change management, adoption, implementation of AI-native solutions.

• Owning client or stakeholder relationships end to end, with real accountability for outcomes

• Product, programme or engagement leadership in a technical environment

• Being technically literate - fluent enough in data and AI to make the right calls and earn trust with both buyers and builders, without needing to write the production code yourself

• Translating between business strategy and what's actually buildable

• Bringing structure to ambiguous, fast-moving situations

• The patience to sit with a worried manager, and the stubbornness to stay until adoption actually lands

Curiosity, taste and the way you think matter just as much to us as specific tools or years of experience. We hire for the who, not the what - experience is an indicator of perspective, not a deciding factor for how senior a role you'll play here. We're hiring across levels and shape the role around the person.

Why Heyra

At Heyra, we believe consulting needs to be rewritten. We're building a consultancy designed for the agentic era. We design, build, and operate AI products that change how enterprises work - from problem to prototype to production.

We care deeply about craft, speed and building things that work in the real world.

Heyra brings together people from engineering, strategy, product, startup and creative environments. We keep teams small, collaboration close and momentum high.

**You'll Join a Team Where

**

• people care deeply about what they build

• good ideas move quickly

• new technology gets explored early

• and where there is room to shape both the company and the way we work

We're around 50 people today after merging with Pyne, and we're only just getting started.

If owning how AI engagements get framed, sold and landed at Heyra sounds like your kind of work, send us a short note about yourself together with your CV. We care much more about curiosity, energy and the way you think than polished applications.

**Benefits

**

• Healthcare insurance

• Pension plan

• Parental leave

• Social gatherings

• New tech gear

• Central office

• Free lunch, coffee, snacks, and Friday beers

• Skill development

• Paid holiday

• Remote work allowed

• Pet friendly

Would you like to lead and further develop the Finance function at Denmark’s largest refinery? Kalundborg Refinery is seeking an experienced Head of Finance to combine hands-on operational finance leadership with strategic influence on site performance.

The high requirements for safety, operational reliability and regulatory compliance in a critical industrial environment require strong financial leadership, clear governance and the ability to create effective collaboration across site operations and Group functions.

Kalundborg Refinery is critical infrastructure within Denmark’s energy supply system and accounts for more than 15% of the country’s total energy consumption. Since January 2022, the refinery has been part of Klesch Group and operates alongside a sister site in Heide, Germany, and a recently acquired refinery in Gelsenkirchen, also in Germany. Under Klesch Group ownership, Kalundborg Refinery continues to operate with an uncompromising focus on safe and reliable operations, operational excellence and long-term value creation.

As Head of Finance, you will lead the full Finance function at Kalundborg Refinery and act as the primary financial steward and business partner to the Site Managing Director. You will be closely connected to Group and report to the Group CFO, ensuring alignment with Group finance standards, controls and reporting. As a member of the Leadership Team, you will contribute to the Company’s overall business strategy and take responsibility for both day-to-day operations and strategic initiatives across Finance.

You will have overall leadership and management responsibility for Controlling, Accounting, budgeting and Tax in Kalundborg. Your key responsibilities include:

• Ensuring effective and efficient management and execution of all finance-related matters.

• Ensuring operational excellence within Finance and compliance with applicable requirements and Company policies.

• Overseeing quarterly financial reporting and the preparation of annual financial statements, ensuring clean, credible and on-time reporting with no material control gaps.

• Overseeing and monitoring relevant direct and indirect tax matters.

• Preparing monthly management information for the shareholder and senior leadership team. Ensuring an effective and timely monthly financial close.

• Driving the budgeting process in Kalundborg with close coordination with project managers and Group.

• Supporting the management of structured finance arrangements, including preparation for and participation in bank calls, liquidity planning and liquidity monitoring.

• Leading and developing the Finance team, strengthening KPI dashboard reporting and building clear succession visibility.

The right candidate has:

• A degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or a related field, combined with 8–12+ years of finance experience in multinational and manufacturing or industrial environments.

• A track record of leading a Finance team of comparable size, approximately 10–15 employees, at plant or site level.

• Strong command of IFRS and experience with financial reporting; consolidated reporting experience is an advantage.

• Experience with cost accounting, standard costing, capex appraisal, ERP systems — preferably SAP or equivalent — and advanced financial modelling and analysis.

• Fluency in a Scandinavian language and professional proficiency in English.

• The ability to operate confidently as a peer to plant operations leadership and manage stakeholders effectively across a dual reporting structure.

• Demonstrates dynamism and a continuous drive for results.

• Attention to detail and ability to present complex matters in a simple way.

• A demonstrated ability to develop and retain an engaged Finance team, communicate difficult financial truths with commercial tact and build strong functional capability.

The position is based in Kalundborg, Denmark. Travel (app. 2 days per month) is to be expected.

Would you like to know more?

Please review the detailed Assignment Brief before contacting Mercuri Urval for a confidential discussion with director Thomas Gajhede, MU (+45 2084 1030).

Application deadline: December 2, 2026

Aarhus Airport is hiring an Analyst (Route Development & Marketing)

Aarhus Airport is growing – this year we are seeing a record number of passengers enjoy the very best customer experience of Denmark’s fastest growing airport while traveling to and from a widening number of destinations with our airline and tour operator partners. Can you see the next new opportunity and identify the latest trends to influence where customers will fly and how they get there? We will be welcoming more partners, destinations and guests, making use of ever-developing airport amenities that require planning, analysis and performance monitoring. To help us do so, we are looking for a new and talented colleague to join the strategic team that leads our route development, marketing and communications work. Energetically researching, monitoring, analysing and determining the data and insight that powers our planning and harnessing of valuable air capacity for Aarhus and the region, if you would like to be part of the team that shapes this connectivity strategy for the Nordic region’s fifth most populous metro area, to bring millions of customers to thousands of flights that service Aarhus Airport now and in the years to come, we want to hear from you.

Our ideal Analyst will be able to join as soon as possible and get to work on carrying-out market analysis of both existing and new potential routes, with both existing and future airline and tour operator partners. This opportunity is located at our brand-new offices at Aarhus Airport and will be an integral part of our team-spirited wider airport family, working across the organisation as required.

In this position your primary areas of responsibility will include:

• Analysing existing routes, potential routes and aviation market data, supporting work in growing passenger throughput, generating business cases and providing valuable data to the Route Development, Marketing & Communications team

• Helping attract and win new airline services, tour operators and air freight providers among other business development opportunities by way of sharp and investigative analysis

• Work astutely with market intelligence and data – from reporting, analysing, market-sizing and trend development, to identifying, researching and underpinning new business opportunity by smartly applying business acumen

• Develop a grasp and detailed understanding of population dynamics, socio-economic, migration and immigration as well as regional economic trends across Denmark and applicable international communities, as well as trade and tourism

• Using both new and available data and analytical methodology, support the commercial activity, sales, marketing and communication initiatives of the organisation

• Produce, research and maintain analytical and insight tools to help optimally showcase Aarhus Airport’s market, regional economy and destination assets

• Support the knowledge-building of AAR’s work in economic, aviation and wider industry trends

• Support work with stakeholders and business partners from around the industry and region including tourism partners, corporate customers, airlines and tour operator partners

• Assist with applicable project management and business development by way of competent planning, modelling, budgeting and forecasting

• Assist in commercial calculations, analysis and negotiations with management and leadership, in pursuit of incremental revenue sustainability and asset optimisation

• Co-operate closely with marketing, communications, administration, customer service and operational colleagues

• Attend and support airline and tour operator negotiations as required, including attendance of industry conferences, conventions and exhibitions. The role involves some international travel which should appeal to your general wanderlust and passion for travel, tourism and/or aviation

The right candidate will, among other attributes, demonstrate that they have:

• Strong skill sets in analytical, business and/or commercial arena and ideally some international work experience, or a very significant interest in this field. Perhaps you have worked in travel already or are keen to do so, maybe an interest in airport, airline and the travel sector in general

• A business degree of relevance with a lean towards statistical, data and analytical strengths, possibly within business, economics, marketing, communications or another commercial discipline

• Fluency in English, perhaps a Scandinavian language too. Additional languages are an advantage

• A head for numbers, strong IT and excellent interpersonal communication skills are a must. Fully competent in excel, powerpoint, other IT suites and data tools, where thinking outside of the box, challenging assumptions with evidence and insight, above all being inquisitive and solution-oriented are second nature

• The ability to work confidently and in a structured way with extensive data material and in detail, producing meaningful analysis, reports, proposals and delivering valuable insight to colleagues and decision-makers. At the same time you are able to work independently and as part of a team, tie dynamic data and insight together and present complex data in an attractive way, visually and verbally

• The ability to gain security clearance from the Danish Police, hold a valid passport and have or obtain the right to live and work in Aarhus, Denmark is a minimum requirement.

Aarhus Airport offers a range of benefits in line with qualifications and experience. We have towering ambitions for the future and invite you to join us if the above snapshot is a fit and you are keen to contribute in building the region’s future international connectivity, and the potential to develop your career with us excites you. We are an equal opportunities employer and an organisation that likes to stand out from the crowd, we thrive on excellence and diversity within our team regardless of background, ethnicity, gender or sexual orientation. We expect the review of applications and interviews to be ongoing until the position is filled, and encourage you to reach out as soon as possible if the opportunity resonates.

We look forward to receiving your CV and covering letter with an indication of salary expectations via the application link on our website. If you have any questions, feel free to contact us by email at dsu@aar.dk

A day in your life with us

Are you ready to be the one who saves the customers’ day – right in the middle of their shopping trip?

At IKEA, it’s not just about furniture – it’s about experiences. We are looking for someone who wants to make it quick, easy, and enjoyable for our customers to take a well-deserved break with great food.

You will become part of an enthusiastic team that supports each other, has fun, and creates space for you to be yourself. We will provide thorough training so you can feel confident in the role.

The position is an average of 12 or 15 hours per week. Your working hours will vary depending on the needs of the business, with shifts scheduled between 09:00AM–20:45PM. On weekdays, your shift will typically start at 16:00PM. We all work 5 out of 8 weekends.

Your tasks will include:

• Working as part of our dishwasher team.

• Cleaning and maintaining a high hygiene standard, ensuring that all plates, glasses, and other tableware are in perfect condition for our customers.

• Working with routines in a fast-paced environment.

Why we will love you

Your background can be diverse – what matters most is that you are ready for a physically active job, are service-minded, full of energy, and able to make things happen!

As a dishwasher at IKEA Food, you thrive on routine tasks, and it is an advantage if you:

• Are used to working in a fast-paced environment.

• Have experience maintaining a high level of hygiene.

• Have worked in a similar role before.

• Speak basic Danish or basic English.

Questions and support? Let's connect!

If you have any questions, please contact Food Operations Manager Barsha Gurung, barsha.gurung@ingka.ikea.com. Please note that we do not accept applications via e-mail but only through our recruitment portal.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position at the Department of Law, University of Southern Denmark (SDU) Religious Education, Legal Consciousness and Social Cohesion in Post-Imperial Islamic Societies
jobs.description:
The Department of Law at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a fully funded three-year PhD position within the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network MINARET – Islamic Legal Cultures in Post-Imperial Contexts. Employment is expected to begin September 1, 2027, or by agreement.

The successful candidate will be enrolled in the PhD School at SDU Business School and the Faculty of Social Sciences and employed at the Department of Law, University of Southern Denmark.

 

About the MINARET Doctoral Network

MINARET is an international doctoral network funded through the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA). The network investigates how Islamic legal cultures shape governance, citizenship, institutions and everyday legal practices across post-imperial societies.

The programme brings together universities and non-academic partners across Europe, North Africa, Central Asia and Southeast Asia. Doctoral candidates will receive interdisciplinary training, international supervision and extensive mobility opportunities.

Further information about the network is available at MINARET website.

 

Project Description

This doctoral project examines how constitutional and legal frameworks governing religious education shape citizenship, legal consciousness and social cohesion in Indonesia and Morocco.

The project investigates how constitutional values, religious identities and civic norms are translated into educational practices and everyday experiences of citizenship. Particular attention is paid to how religious education influences democratic participation, social integration and perceptions of rights, duties and belonging.

The project contributes to research on legal consciousness, sociology of law, citizenship studies and comparative constitutionalism. Through comparative empirical research in Indonesia and Morocco, the doctoral candidate will analyse how educational institutions function as sites where legal norms, religious values and civic identities intersect.

The candidate is expected to develop an original research design within the overall framework of the project.

 

Host Institution

The position is based at the Department of Law, University of Southern Denmark, Denmark.

The Department of Law is part of the Faculty of Social Sciences and hosts a vibrant interdisciplinary environment within sociology of law, legal anthropology, human rights and comparative legal studies.

The successful candidate will become part of the department’s research environment as well as the international MINARET doctoral network.

More information about our PhD programme is available at the department’s website. On the website, you will also find the department’s qualifications criteria. The programme is provided by the PhD School at SDU Business School and the Faculty of Social Sciences who offer further information on their website.

 

Supervision

The doctoral candidate will be supervised by:

• 
Professor Ole Hammerslev (University of Southern Denmark) (principal supervisor)

• 
Co-supervisor from MINARET consortium

Additional mentoring and supervision will be provided through the MINARET network.

 

Fieldwork and Mobility

The project includes substantial international mobility.

The doctoral candidate is expected to conduct fieldwork in:

• 
Indonesia

• 
Morocco

 

In addition, the candidate will undertake two secondments within the MINARET network:

• 
one academic secondment at a partner university;

• 
one non-academic secondment with a relevant partner organisation.

 

Participation in network-wide training events, workshops, summer schools and conferences is mandatory.

 

Tasks and Responsibilities

The successful candidate will:

• 
conduct independent doctoral research within the project framework;

• 
participate actively in the MINARET doctoral network;

• 
undertake international fieldwork and secondments;

• 
complete PhD courses and training activities;

• 
contribute to the research environment at the Department of Law;

• 
participate in teaching and related activities in accordance with Danish PhD regulations.

 

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must hold a relevant master’s degree (or equivalent) in law, sociology, political science, anthropology, religious studies, education, or a related social science discipline.

Applicants must meet the admission requirements of the PhD School at SDU Business School and the Faculty of Social Sciences, SDU, which you can learn more about on the PhD School’s website. 

Applicants must also meet requirements in accordance with the MSCA Doctoral Network:

• 
applicants must not already hold a doctoral degree;

• 
applicants must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the recruitment date.

Excellent English language skills are required.

 

Desired Qualifications

Preference will be given to applicants with documented experience or interest in one or more of the following areas:

• 
sociology of law;

• 
legal consciousness;

• 
citizenship studies;

• 
religion and law;

• 
Islamic legal cultures;

• 
qualitative and comparative research methods;

• 
fieldwork-based research.

 

Knowledge of Arabic, Bahasa Indonesia, French or other relevant languages is an advantage but not a requirement.

 

Assessment Criteria

Applicants will be assessed on:

• 
academic qualifications (please consult the guidelines for recognizing merit at the Department of Law);

• 
quality and feasibility of the proposed research project;

• 
methodological competencies;

• 
motivation and suitability for international and interdisciplinary research;

• 
ability to contribute to the objectives of the MINARET doctoral network.

 

We Offer

The position offers:

• 
Three years of full-time employment as a PhD fellow at SDU;

• 
enrolment in an internationally recognised PhD programme;

• 
participation in a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network;

• 
international supervision and training;

• 
research mobility and secondments;

• 
competitive salary and employment conditions in accordance with Danish regulations and MSCA provisions.

 

Contact information

For more information about the department and the position, please contact Head of Department, Ole Hammerslev, ohv@sam.sdu.dk. 

 

Terms of employment      
The applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) for academics in the state sector, including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at universities and the regulations for PhD students as described therein.

Employment as a PhD student is subject to the circular of 20 December 2021, on the agreement for academics in the state sector – Appendix 5, protocol on PhD students.

The person employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a self-organiser.

Salary and employment terms

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements.

As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process.

SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.

 

The assessment and evaluation process

Shortlisting may be used in the assessment process. Please note that only shortlisted applicants will receive an assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee and the shortlisted applicants will receive the part of the evaluation that concerns them. The committee may request additional information, and if so, it is the responsibility of the applicants to provide the necessary material.

Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. 

 

Application   

 

The application must include the following:

•   Motivated application
•   Detailed Curriculum vitae (educational and work history should be specified by month and year)
•   A certified copy of your master’s degree certificate, including transcripts of all examination results – alternatively, the expected date to finish the master’s degree. Foreign diplomas that are not in Norwegian, Swedish or English must be accompanied by a translation into Danish or English, as well as a translation of the official description of the marking scale used. 
•   An application form (is available here)
•   A project description (max 5 pages of 2,400 characters each, including spaces, notes, appendices, bibliography etc.). The guidelines for preparing a PhD project proposal for the Department of Law are available here.
•   An abstract of the project description of no more than 250 words
•   Publications, if any – however, no more than two. If one of the attached publications is a master thesis, only the problem formulation and the conclusion should be attached, not the entire thesis.
•   Information on teaching experience or other forms of academic communication.

Documents which are not in Danish, Norwegian or Swedish must be translated into English. SDU may discard applications which are incomplete regarding the above-mentioned criteria without further notice. All documents must be in pdf format, no more than 5 MB per file. 

Documents should not contain a CPR number (civil registration number) – in this case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

Applicants are encouraged to read the information "How to apply" before applying. If you experience technical problems when uploading the application, please contact hcm-support@sdu.dk. 

UPLOAD GUIDE: Motivated application should be uploaded as ‘Cover letter’, Curriculum Vitae should be uploaded as ‘Resume’. All other documents should be uploaded as ‘Miscellaneous documents’. 

 

The application deadline is January 31, 2027, 23.59 CET/CEST.

 Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now" on our website.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.

 

About SDU

The University of Southern Denmark was established to create value for and with society. Whether our contributions come in the form of excellent research, innovative solutions, education or learning, we must make a positive difference to society and contribute to a sustainable future. We do this by cultivating talents and creating the best environments for research and learning. It is therefore crucial that SDU retains, develops and recruits talent. At the same time, we need to ensure consistently high quality in all our activities – and we can only do that with the right people. The University’s researchers, lecturers, students, managers and technical/administrative staff are the foundation of our success.
